title: What Would You Sacrifice for Gains? (An Essay on Ambition & Selfishness)
summary: Philosophical essay using Toguro from Yu Yu Hakusho as a Faustian character to analyse why young lifters sacrifice health for gains via PEDs. NH argues that PED use is a self-denying, selfish Faustian bargain driven by fear of underachievement and kept going by the sunk-cost fallacy, and contrasts it with Yusuke's life-affirming egoism (amor fati).
claims: Dismissing PED users as simply stupid or evil does not help; the temptation is real and must be understood logically, not moralistically
Taking PEDs is a bad thing but does not make someone a bad person; users are misguided
He promotes becoming better, not feeling better by drawing moral lines between naturals and users
PED use starts as a means to a dream but becomes an end in itself; the dream keeps growing so the drugs never stop
A finite dream disappoints once reached; an evolving, unreasonable dream keeps you going
Young lifters are driven by fear of underachievement and wasting youth, believing it is too late after 25, which pushes them to trade their best years for gains
When weighing a sacrifice for selfish gains like PEDs, look at what you would lose, not only what you would gain
PEDs are a basic Faustian bargain: trading vitality and longevity for muscle; any deal with the devil satisfies short term but costs more long term
PED users dying on camera often cannot stop because of the sunk-cost fallacy: quitting would admit past sacrifices were for nothing
Enhanced users who promote drugs pull others into the same bargain to justify their own choice
'See the muscles you could have built' is the PED users' pitch to naturals, and it is very seductive to the young
TRT at 25 and anti-aging obsession are forms of rejecting life rather than accepting aging
Dogmatic fitness YouTubers are not dumb; they choose closed-mindedness ('will to stupidity') because constant doubt is hard
Judge a morality by whether you can live with its consequences; accept outcomes as part of your journey (amor fati)
Sacrifice is not automatically virtuous or selfless; many sacrifices are selfish and stupid
The healthiest stance is egoism (putting your welfare first while caring about those who matter) rather than self-denial
In his poll most viewers would sacrifice nothing for gains; 8% would sacrifice relationships or soul, only 1% health, ironic since health is what PED users lose
